content.user_title: Build Scalable PyTorch Lightning Training Workflows
content.value_statement: Deep learning projects become difficult to maintain when training, data, logging, and scaling logic are mixed. This skill provides structured PyTorch Lightning guidance and templates.
actual_capabilities: Structures models as LightningModules with training, validation, testing, prediction, and optimizer methods.
Organizes dataset preparation and DataLoaders with reusable LightningDataModules.
Configures Trainers for debugging, mixed precision, checkpoints, early stopping, and gradient controls.
Explains TensorBoard, Weights and Biases, MLflow, Neptune, Comet, and CSV logging.
Compares DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed strategies for single-node and multi-node training.
Provides Python templates for model modules, data modules, and common Trainer configurations.
limitations: The templates require adaptation for each model architecture, dataset, loss function, and metric.
The skill does not run training jobs or provision GPU infrastructure.
Distributed examples require compatible hardware, installed dependencies, and cluster configuration.
Logger integrations require separate service accounts, packages, and secure credential management.

use_cases.title: Structure a Research Prototype
use_cases.description: Convert a manual PyTorch loop into clear model, data, validation, logging, and optimizer components.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Training Code
use_cases.description: Create reusable project templates with consistent callbacks, checkpoints, metrics, and data handling.

use_cases.title: Scale Large Training Jobs
use_cases.description: Select and configure DDP, FSDP, or DeepSpeed for available accelerators and model size.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PyTorch LightningModule for [task] using [model], [loss], and [optimizer]. Include training and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Data Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LightningDataModule for [dataset]. Include preparation, stage-aware setup, transforms, splits, and configurable DataLoaders.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Production Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure a Trainer for [hardware] with mixed precision, checkpoints, early stopping, gradient clipping, logging, and reproducibility.

prompt_templates.title: Design Distributed Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed for [model size] on [cluster]. Recommend a strategy and explain memory, speed, and operational tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Convert a classifier training loop into PyTorch Lightning.
output_examples.output: A LightningModule outline separates forward, training, validation, testing, metrics, and optimizer configuration. It also identifies required project-specific replacements.

output_examples.input: Recommend settings for training a large transformer on eight GPUs.
output: Use FSDP when model parameters exceed practical single-device memory.
Enable mixed precision and activation checkpointing after checking model compatibility.
Validate the setup with a short development run before full training.

output_examples.input: Add experiment tracking and reliable checkpoints.
output_examples.output: A Trainer plan combines one selected logger, monitored checkpoints, early stopping, learning-rate tracking, and reduced logging frequency.

best_practices: Start with a short development run before increasing epochs, devices, or dataset size.
Keep data preparation, model logic, callbacks, and logging responsibilities separate.
Store service credentials outside source code and inject them through supported secret management.
anti_patterns: Do not set state in prepare_data because distributed workers do not receive that state.
Do not use device-specific calls when Lightning can manage device placement.
Do not enable complex distributed strategies before validating single-device correctness.

faq.question: Does this skill install PyTorch Lightning?
faq.answer: No. Install compatible PyTorch and Lightning packages in your environment before using generated project code.

faq.question: Can it convert an existing PyTorch training loop?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the model, loss, optimizer, data loading, and evaluation logic for a structured conversion.

faq.question: Which distributed strategies are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, multi-node setup, SLURM, and common troubleshooting guidance.

faq.question: Does it support experiment tracking?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents TensorBoard, Weights and Biases, MLflow, Neptune, Comet, and CSV loggers.

faq.question: Will the templates work without changes?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholder models, datasets, losses, metrics, and resource settings with project-specific implementations.

faq.question: Does the skill manage API keys?
faq.answer: No. Use environment variables or a secret manager and follow each logging provider's secure configuration guidance.
